This is a genuine race condition:\n///\n/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n///\n/// This is most common with:\n/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n///\n/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use this helper\n///\n/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n/// disk immediately before execution:\n///\n/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n///\n/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n///\n/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n///     || async {\n///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n///             .arg(\"--version\")\n///             .output()\n///             .await\n///     },\n///     5,\n///     20,\n/// ).await?;\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child<F, Fut>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms).await\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n///\n/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n///\n/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n///\n/// Use exponential backoff when:\n/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n///\n/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n///\n/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n///     || async {\n///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n///             .arg(\"--version\")\n///             .output()\n///             .await\n///     },\n///     10,\n///     20,\n/// ).await?;\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n\n                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n\n                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n                let delay = exponential_delay\n                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned process\n/// (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential_child<F, Fut>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms).await\n}\n\n// ─── Synchronous ETXTBSY retry helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This is the sync equivalent of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`, using `std::thread::sleep`\n/// instead of `tokio::time::sleep`. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n      max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of The retry logic handles the race condition where a\n/// binary written to disk moments earlier (e.g., during upgrade or test setup)\n/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\" (errno 26).\nasync fn spawn_version_check(br_path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Output> {\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n        || async {\n            tokio::process::Command::new(br_path)\n                .arg(\"--version\")\n                .output()\n                .await\n        },\n        5,\n        20,\n    )\n    .await\n}\n\n/// Check the bead-forge version and detect known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This function runs `bf --version` and parses the output to detect\n/// versions with known bugs. The primary use case is detecting bead-forge\n/// 0.2.0, which has a bug where `--limit 0` returns an empty set instead\n/// of all beads.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// - `VersionCheck::Ok` if the version is not known to be bad\n/// - `VersionCheck::KnownBad` if a known-bad version is detected\n/// - `VersionCheck::Failed` if the version check failed\npub async fn check_bead_forge_version(br_path: &Path) -> VersionCheck {\n    let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n\n    let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, spawn_version_check(br_path)).await {\n        Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n        Ok(Err(e)) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: format!(\"failed to spawn bf --version: {e}\"),\n            };\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: \"bf --version timed out after 5s\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n    };\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"bf --version exited with code {}\",\n                output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let version = stdout.trim().to_string();\n\n    if version.is_empty() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: \"bf --version produced no output\".to_string(),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Extract version number by taking the second word if present\n    // This handles formats like \"bf 0.2.0\" or \"br 0.2.0-github\"\n    let version_number = version.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or(&version);\n\n    // Check against known-bad version prefixes\n    let mut issues = Vec::new();\n    for &(bad_prefix, issue) in KNOWN_BAD_VERSIONS {\n        if version_number.starts_with(bad_prefix) {\n            issues.push(issue.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !issues.is_empty() {\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues }\n    } else {\n        VersionCheck::Ok\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run version handshake and emit telemetry for known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This is called during worker boot to detect and warn about known-bad\n/// bead-forge versions. It emits a WARN-level telemetry event if issues\n/// are found.\npub async fn run_version_handshake(br_path: &Path) {\n    match check_bead_forge_version(br_path).await {\n        VersionCheck::Ok => {\n            tracing::debug!(\"bead-forge version check passed\");\n        }\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues } => {\n            for issue in &issues {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    version = %version,\n                    issue = %issue,\n                    \"bead-forge version has known bugs — explicit limits will be used to work around\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        VersionCheck::Failed { reason } => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                reason = %reason,\n                \"failed to check bead-forge version — cannot detect known-bad versions\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Corruption detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Known error strings that   /// Whether an error indicates a sync conflict according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_sync_conflict(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// List all beads with no incomplete blockers (ready to work on).\n    ///\n    /// Returns an empty `Vec` when the queue is empty — that is not an error.\n    /// Returns `Err` if JSON parsing or br invocation fails.\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// List ALL beads in the workspace (no readiness/filter checks).\n    ///\n    /// Used by Knot strand for three-state verification — a DIFFERENT code\n    /// path from `ready()` to avoid v1's false-positive bug.\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// Fetch a single bead by ID.\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>;\n\n    /// Fetch a bead together with the number of claim-related history entries\n    /// the backend exposed for it.\n    ///\n    /// Most backends do not include event history in their normal bead\n    /// projection, so the default implementation reports no count.  A\n    /// backend that does expose history can override this to let NEEDLE stop\n    /// retrying a bead before another claim mutation grows its JSON record.\n    async fn show_with_claim_history(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<(Bead, Option<u32>)> {\n        Ok((self.show(id).await?, None))\n    }\n\n    /// Fetch operator/agent notes when the backend exposes them.\n    ///\n    /// Backends without a notes projection return `None`; this keeps notes a\n    /// capability rather than forcing it into NEEDLE's common bead model.\n    async fn notes(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Option<String>> {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt to atomically claim a bead (set status=in_progress, assignee=actor).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `RaceLost { claimed_by }` — another worker got there first.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — bead not in a claimable state.\n    async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Atomically find and claim the next available bead (server-selected).\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios as it eliminates\n    /// race conditions: the server selects the bead and assigns it in a single\n    /// BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked (e.g., after it exceeds the\n    /// consecutive-failure threshold in `OutcomeConfig::quarantine_after_failures`).\n    ///\n    /// Unlike `release`, this deliberately does NOT clear the assignee or return\n    /// the bead to a claimable state — the whole point is to stop Pluck from\n    /// re-selecting it until a human (or a future auto-split) intervenes.\n    async fn block(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Clear the assignee on a bead without changing its status.\n    ///\n    /// Used by mend to heal open beads with stale assignees (e.g., after reopen).\n    async fn clear_assignee(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. This prevents SYNC_CONFLICT\n    /// errors when the JSONL has newer remote changes.\n    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Reopen a closed (Done) bead back to open status.\n    ///\n    /// Used by validation gates when verification fails after an agent has\n    /// already closed the bead.\n    async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// List all labels on a bead.\n    async fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>>;\n\n    /// Add a label to a bead.\n    async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Remove a label from a bead.\n    async fn remove_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Create a new bead and return its ID.\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str, labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId>;\n\n    /// Add a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep add <blocker_id> --blocks <blocked_id>`.\n    async fn add_dependency(&self, blocker_id: &BeadId, blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Atomically create `children` and link each as a blocker of `parent_id`.\n    ///\n    /// This is the \"mitosis\" / bead-splitting primitive. N child creations plus\n    /// N dependency links must commit together: otherwise a crash between the\n    /// `create` and the `dep add` (SIGKILL, OOM, pod eviction) leaves an orphaned\n    /// child with no dependency link, and the parent never unblocks — plan.md\n    /// Phase 5.3, Race 3.\n    ///\n    /// The parent is deliberately **not** closed: NEEDLE keeps a split parent\n    /// open/blocked while its children are worked.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation performs the historical non-atomic sequence\n    /// (`create_bead` + `add_dependency`, one child at a time). Mock stores rely\n    /// on it, and bf-backed stores fall back to it when the atomic path is\n    /// unavailable. Backends that can run a transactional batch (bf) override\n    /// this to make the whole split crash-safe.\n    async fn split_bead(\n        &self,\n        parent_id: &BeadId,\n        children: &[NewChild<'_>],\n    ) -> Result<Vec<BeadId>> {\n        let mut created = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());\n        for child in children {\n            let child_id = self\n                .create_bead(child.title, child.body, child.labels)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create child bead: {}\", child.title))?;\n            self.add_dependency(&child_id, parent_id)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\"failed to add dependency: {child_id} blocks {parent_id}\")\n                })?;\n            created.push(child_id);\n        }\n        Ok(created)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep remove <blocked_id> <blocker_id>`.\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor --repair` and return the report.\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor` (without `--repair`) to check database health.\n    ///\n    /// Returns warnings if any issues are detected, without attempting to fix them.\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Full database rebuild from the configured backend's durable checkpoint.\n    ///\n    /// The existing SQLite file set remains in a rollback backup until the\n    /// public backend import and doctor verification both succeed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if rebuild or verification fails; the original database\n    /// is restored in that case.\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Check if this store has a valid bead store (i.e., has a `.beads/` directory).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` if the workspace contains a `.beads/` directory, `false` otherwise.\n    /// This is used by strands to distinguish between \"no home store configured\" (expected,\n    /// benign for roam-only workers) and \"home store is broken\" (unexpected, problem).\n    fn has_valid_store(&self) -> bool;\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), b\"success\".to_vec());\n        assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn etxtbsy_retry_linear_retries_on_etxtbsy() {\n        let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result: std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    let attempt = count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    if attempt < 2 {\n                        // Fail first 2 attempts with ETXTBSY\n                        Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                    } else {\n                        Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                    }\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), b\"success\".to_vec());\n        assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3); // 2 failures + 1 success\n    }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn etxtbsy_retry_linear_exhausts_attempts() {\n        let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result: std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    // Always fail with ETXTBSY\n                    Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                }\n            },\n            3,\n            20,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        assert!(result.is_err());\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().raw_os_error(), Some(26));\n        assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3); // max attempts\n    }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn etxtbsy_retry_linear_fails_fast_on_non_etxtbsy() {\n        let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result: std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    count.fetch_add(1, This test verifies that jitter actually randomizes delays.\n        // We run the same retry scenario multiple times and verify that\n        // delays vary between runs (not always identical).\n        const BASE_MS: u64 = 20;\n        const NUM_RUNS: usize = 10;\n\n        let mut elapsed_times = Vec::with_capacity(NUM_RUNS);\n\n        for _ in 0..NUM_RUNS {\n            let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n            let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n            let start = Instant::now();\n\n            let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n                || {\n                    let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                    async move {\n                        let attempt = count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                        if attempt < 2 {\n                            // Fail first 2 attempts with ETXTBSY to trigger 2 retry delays\n                            Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                        } else {\n                            Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                        }\n                    }\n                },\n                10,\n                BASE_MS,\n            )\n            .await;\n\n            let elapsed = start.elapsed();\n            elapsed_times.push(elapsed);\n\n            assert!(result.is_ok());\n            assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3); // 2 failures + 1 success\n        }\n\n        // Verify that not all elapsed times are identical (jitter is working)\n        // With ±25% jitter on exponential backoff, times should vary\n        let unique_times: std::collections::HashSet<_> =\n            elapsed_times.iter().map(|d| d.as_millis()).collect();\n\n        // We expect at least some variation across 10 runs\n        // If jitter wasn't working, all times would be identical\n        assert!(\n            unique_times.len() > 1,\n            \"Expected jitter to create varying delays, but got {} unique times out of {} runs: {:?}\",\n            unique_times.len(),\n            NUM_RUNS,\n            elapsed_times\n        );\n\n        // Verify that times stay within reasonable bounds\n        // Expected: 20ms + 40ms = ~60ms with jitter (15-75ms range)\n        for elapsed in &elapsed_times {\n            assert!(\n                *elapsed >= Duration::from_millis(10),\n                \"Elapsed time {} too short (expected >=10ms with jitter)\",\n                elapsed.as_millis()\n            );\n            assert!(\n                *elapsed < Duration::from_millis(150),\n                \"Elapsed time {} too long (expected <150ms with jitter)\",\n                elapsed.as_millis()\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_jitter_randomization() {\n        // Sync version of the jitter randomization test\n        const BASE_MS: u64 = `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// 125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. ```\n    pub fn evaluate(\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        retry_count: u32,\n        bead_body: Option<&String>,\n        has_assignee: bool,\n        is_child_bead: bool,\n        proposals: ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). The aliases\n/// below accept both without changing how bf/br JSON deserializes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    #[serde(alias = \"blocker\")]\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub title: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub status: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    #[serde(rename = \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a bead.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Comment {\n    /// Comment ID (internal database ID).\n    pub id: i64,\n    /// The bead this comment is on.\n    #[serde(rename = \"issue_id\")]\n    pub bead_id: String,\n    /// The comment text.\n    pub text: String,\n    /// Author who created the comment.\n    pub author: String,\n    /// When the comment was created.\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Stored as `description` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"description\")]\n    pub body: Option<String>,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    /// Comments on this bead, returned by `bf show --json`.\n    /// Empty array if no comments or backend doesn't support comments.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub comments: Vec<Comment>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// InputMethod\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How the prompt is passed to the agent binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum InputMethod {\n    /// Write the prompt to the agent's stdin.\n    Stdin,\n    /// Write the prompt to a temp file and pass the path.\n    File {\n        /// Template for the temp file path. `{bead_id}` is substituted.\n        path_template: String,\n    },\n    /// Pass the prompt as a CLI argument.\n    Args {\n        /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Path reference to a worker's heartbeat file on disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeartbeatFile {\n    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,\n}\n\n/// Health status of a peer worker as inferred from its heartbeat file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum PeerStatus {\n    /// Heartbeat is fresh — peer is considered alive.\n    Alive {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat TTL has elapsed — peer may be stuck.\n    Stale {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        claimed_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat file is missing — peer is dead or never started.\n    Dead { heartbeat_file: HeartbeatFile },\n}\n\n// )\n        .unwrap()];\n\n        let decision = DecompositionDecision::evaluate(\n            60,     // 1 minute timeout (below 120s threshold)\n            3,      // sufficient retries\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Diagnosis from the Knot strand when all work-finding strategies are exhausted.\n///\n/// This three-state model prevents false-positive starvation alerts by\n/// distinguishing between \"queue genuinely empty\" vs \"all work claimed by\n/// other workers\" vs \"beads exist but are invisible due to configuration.\"\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ExhaustionDiagnosis {\n    /// No beads exist in the workspace at all — queue is genuinely empty.\n    /// This is normal idle, not an alert condition.\n    NoBeadsExist,\n    /// All beads are claimed by other workers — wait for them to finish.\n    /// This is normal congestion, not an alert condition.\n    AllClaimed,\n    /// Open beads exist but Pluck found none — indicates a config error.\n    /// This is an alert condition: beads may be invisible due to label filters.\n    Invisible,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ExhaustionDiagnosis {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::NoBeadsExist => write!(f, \"no_beads_exist\"),\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::AllClaimed => write!(f, \"all_claimed\"),\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::Invisible => write!(f, \"invisible\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ChildBeadProposal\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A proposal for a child bead to be created during timeout decomposition.\n///\n/// This structure captures all the information needed to propose a new child bead\n/// when a parent bead times out and needs to be decomposed into smaller phases.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ChildBeadProposal {\n    /// Title of the phase (e.g., \"Phase 1: Core Implementation\").\n    pub phase_title: String,\n    /// Detailed description of what this phase accomplishes.\n    pub description: String,\n    /// Parent bead IDs that this child depends on.\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BeadId>,\n    /// Priority level (lower number = higher priority).\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Labels to apply to the child bead.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl ChildBeadProposal {\n    /// Create a new child bead proposal with validation.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `phase_title` - Title of the phase\n    /// * `description` - Detailed description of the phase\n    /// * `dependencies` - Parent bead IDs this child depends on\n    /// * `priority` - Priority level (0-4)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// * `Ok(ChildBeadProposal)` if validation passes\n    /// * `Err(String)` if validation fails\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::{ChildBeadProposal, BeadId, Priority};\n    ///\n    /// let proposal = ChildBeadProposal::new(\n    ///     \"Phase 1: Core\".to_string(),\n    ///     \"Implement core functionality\".to_string(),\n    ///     vec![BeadId::from(\"needle-parent\")],\n    ///     2,\n    /// ).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn new(\n        phase_title: String,\n        description: String,\n        dependencies: Vec<BeadId>,\n        priority: Priority,\n    ) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        // Validate required fields\n        if phase_title.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"phase_title cannot be empty\".to_string());\n        }\n        if description.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"description cannot be empty\".to_string());\n        }\n        if dependencies.is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"dependencies must contain at least one parent bead ID\".to_string());\n        }\n        if priority > 4 {\n            return Err(\"priority must be between 0 and 4\".to_string());\n        }\n\n        Ok(ChildBeadProposal {\n            phase_title,\n            description,\n            dependencies,\n            priority,\n            labels: Vec::new(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Add labels to the proposal.\n    pub fn with_labels(mut self, labels: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        self.labels = labels;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Validate that all required fields are present and well-formed.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {\n        if self.phase_title.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"phase_title cannot be empty\".to_string());\n        }\n        if self.description.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"description cannot be empty\".to_string());\n        }\n        if self.dependencies.is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"dependencies must contain at least one parent bead ID\".to_string());\n        }\n        if self.priority > 4 {\n            return Err(\"priority must be between 0 and 4\".to_string());\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo test output capture\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Captured output from a cargo test execution.\n///\n/// This struct contains the complete output from running `cargo test`,\n/// including stdout, stderr, exit code, and duration. It is designed to be\n/// serializable for storage and transmission.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::types::OutputCapture;\n/// use std::time::Duration;\n///\n/// let capture = OutputCapture {\n///     stdout: \"running 1 test\\ntest test_foo ... ok\".to_string(),\n///     stderr: String::new(),\n///     exit_code: Some(0),\n///     duration: Duration::from_millis(1500),\n/// };\n///\n/// assert!(capture.success());\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct OutputCapture {\n    /// Captured stdout from the test execution.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Captured stderr from the test execution.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Exit code from the test process. `None` if killed by signal.\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test execution.\n    #[serde(with = \"serde_duration\")]\n    pub duration: Duration,\n}\n\nimpl OutputCapture {\n    /// Returns true if the test exited with code 0.\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the test failed (non-zero exit code).\n    pub fn failed(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.success()\n    }\n\n    /// Get the duration as milliseconds.\n    pub fn duration_ms(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.duration.as_millis() as u64\n    }\n\n    /// Get the total length of stdout and stderr in bytes.\n    pub fn total_output_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.stdout.len() + self.stderr.len()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Serde serialization module for Duration.\n///\n/// Duration is serialized as milliseconds (u64) for JSON compatibility.\nmod serde_duration {\n    use std::time::Duration;\n\n    use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};\n\n    pub fn serialize<S>(duration: &Duration, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>\n    where\n        S: Serializer,\n    {\n        let millis = duration.as_millis() as u64;\n        millis.serialize(serializer)\n    }\n\n    pub fn deserialize<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Duration, D::Error>\n    where\n        D: Deserializer<'de>,\n    {\n        let millis = u64::deserialize(deserializer)?;\n        Ok(Duration::from_millis(millis))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Classification of error types in the build/test pipeline.\n///\n/// Used to categorize errors by their source and recovery path.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ErrorType {\n    /// Error from compiling Rust code (cargo build / cargo test --no-run).\n    Compile,\n    /// Error from running tests (cargo test execution failure).\n    Test,\n    /// Error type could not be determined.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ErrorType {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ErrorType::Compile => write!(f, \"compile\"),\n            ErrorType::Test => write!(f, \"test\"),\n            ErrorType::Unknown => write!(f, \"unknown\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single compilation error detected from cargo test output.\n///\n/// Represents a Rust compiler error with code, message, and optional file location.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum CompilationError {\n    /// A Rust compiler error with error code (e.g., E0308).\n    RustError {\n        /// The error code (e.g., \"E0308\").\n        code: String,\n        /// The error message.\n        message: String,\n        /// Optional file path where the error occurred.\n        file: Option<String>,\n        /// Optional line number where the error occurred.\n        line: Option<usize>,\n        /// Optional column number where the error occurred.\n        column: Option<usize>,\n    },\n    /// General compilation failure without specific error code.\n    General {\n        /// Description of the failure.\n        message: String,\n    },\n    /// Abort message indicating the number of errors.\n    Abort {\n        /// Number of errors that caused the abort.\n        error_count: usize,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl CompilationError {\n    /// Returns a human-readable description of the error.\n    pub fn description(&self) -> String {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError { code, message, .. } => {\n                format!(\"{}: {}\", code, message)\n            }\n            CompilationError::General { message } => message.clone(),\n            CompilationError::Abort { error_count } => {\n                format!(\"aborting due to {} previous error(s)\", error_count)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the error code if this is a Rust compiler error.\n    pub fn error_code(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError { code, .. } => Some(code),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this error has a file location.\n    pub fn has_location(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, CompilationError::RustError { file: Some(_), .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the file location as \"file:line:column\" if available.\n    pub fn location_string(&self) -> Option<String> {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError {\n                file, line, column, ..\n            } => {\n                if let Some(f) = file {\n                    let mut loc = f.clone();\n                    if let Some(l) = line {\n                        loc.push(':');\n                        loc.push_str(&l.to_string());\n                        if let Some(c) = column {\n                            loc.push(':');\n                            loc.push_str(&c.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Some(loc)\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for CompilationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError {\n                code,\n                message,\n                file: _,\n                line: _,\n                column: _,\n            } => {\n                if let Some(loc) = self.location_string() {\n                    write!(f, \"error[{}][{}]: {}\", code, loc, message)\n                } else {\n                    write!(f, \"error[{}]: {}\", code, message)\n                }\n            }\n            CompilationError::General { message } => write!(f, \"{}\", message),\n            CompilationError::Abort { error_count } => {\n                write!(f, \"aborting due to {} previous error(s)\", error_count)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Error Code Classification\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Category of a Rust compiler error code.\n///\n/// Rust error codes (E0XXX) are categorized by their error type to enable\n/// better error handling and reporting.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ErrorCategory {\n    /// Type mismatch errors (E0308, E0309, etc.)\n    TypeMismatch,\n    /// Borrow checker and lifetime errors (E0382, E0502, E0507, etc.)\n    BorrowChecker,\n    /// Missing or incorrect trait implementation (E0038, E0046, etc.)\n    TraitImpl,\n    /// Pattern matching errors (E0002, E0009, etc.)\n    PatternMatching,\n    /// Scope and visibility errors (E0403, E0412, E0603, etc.)\n    ScopeVisibility,\n    /// Syntax errors (E0053, E0063, E0263, etc.)\n    Syntax,\n    /// Generic and const parameter errors (E0207, E0392, E0408, etc.)\n    Generic,\n    /// Macro expansion errors (E0276, E0519, E0704, etc.)\n    Macro,\n    /// Dead code or unused item warnings treated as errors (E0382, E0425, E0526)\n    DeadCode,\n    /// Error code without a standard mapping.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\nimpl ErrorCategory {\n    /// Get a human-readable description of the category.\n    pub fn description(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ErrorCategory::TypeMismatch => \"type mismatch or conversion error\",\n            ErrorCategory::BorrowChecker => \"borrow checker or lifetime error\",\n            ErrorCategory::TraitImpl => \"trait implementation or bound error\",\n            ErrorCategory::PatternMatching => \"pattern matching error\",\n            ErrorCategory::ScopeVisibility => \"scope or visibility error\",\n            ErrorCategory::Syntax => \"syntax error\",\n            ErrorCategory::Generic => \"generic or const parameter error\",\n            ErrorCategory::Macro => \"macro expansion error\",\n            ErrorCategory::DeadCode => \"dead code or unused item\",\n            ErrorCategory::Unknown => \"unknown error category\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ErrorCategory {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ErrorCategory::TypeMismatch => write!(f, \"type_mismatch\"),\n            ErrorCategory::BorrowChecker => write!(f, \"borrow_checker\"),\n            ErrorCategory::TraitImpl => write!(f, \"trait_impl\"),\n            ErrorCategory::PatternMatching => write!(f, \"pattern_matching\"),\n            ErrorCategory::ScopeVisibility => write!(f, \"scope_visibility\"),\n            ErrorCategory::Syntax => write!(f, \"syntax\"),\n            ErrorCategory::Generic => write!(f, \"generic\"),\n            ErrorCategory::Macro => write!(f, \"macro\"),\n            ErrorCategory::DeadCode => write!(f, \"dead_code\"),\n            ErrorCategory::Unknown => write!(f, \"unknown\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse and validate a Rust error code from a string.\n///\n/// This function extracts and validates error codes in the format E0XXX\n/// (where XXX are digits). ────────────���─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Compilation Error Detection\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n///\n/// Parses cargo test stderr output and extracts compilation errors including\n/// error codes, messages, and file locations. Handles multi-line error output\n/// with location information on subsequent lines.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `stderr` - The stderr output from cargo test\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// A vector of `CompilationError` values representing all detected errors.\n/// Returns an empty vector if no compilation errors are detected.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::types::detect_compilation_errors;\n///\n/// let stderr = r#\"error[E0308]: mismatched types\n///  --> src/main.rs:10:5\n///   |\n/// 10|     let x: i32 = \"hello\";\n///   |     ---   ^^^^^^^ expected `i32`, found `&str`\n///   |     expected due to this\n///\n/// error: aborting due to 1 previous error\"#;\n///\n/// let errors = detect_compilation_errors(stderr);\n/// assert_eq!(errors.len(), 1);\n/// assert!(matches!(errors[0], CompilationError::RustError { code, .. } if code == \"E0308\"));\n/// ```\npub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> Vec<CompilationError> {\n    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_error: Option<CompilationError> = None;\n    let mut error_count: Option<usize> = None;\n\n    for line in stderr.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Pattern 1: Rust compiler error with code: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n        if let Some((code, message)) = parse_error_line(line) {\n            // Save any current error before starting a new one\n            if let Some(err) = current_error.take() {\n                errors.push(err);\n            }\n            current_error = Some(CompilationError::RustError {\n                code,\n                message,\n                file: None,\n                line: None,\n                column: None,\n            });\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 2: File location line: \"   --> src/main.rs:10:5\"\n        if current_error.is_some() && line.contains(\"-->\") {\n            if let Some((file, line_num, col)) = parse_location_line(line) {\n                if let Some(CompilationError::RustError {\n                    code,\n                    message,\n                    file: _,\n                    line: _,\n                    column: _,\n                }) = current_error.take()\n                {\n                    current_error = Some(CompilationError::RustError {\n                        code,\n                        message,\n                        file: Some(file),\n                        line: line_num,\n                        column: col,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 3: \"could not compile\" message\n        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n            // Save any current error before adding the general error\n            if let Some(err) = current_error.take() {\n                errors.push(err);\n            }\n            errors.push(CompilationError::General {\n                message: line.to_string(),\n            });\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 4: \"aborting due to N previous errors\"\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") {\n            // Save any current error before processing abort\n            if let Some(err) = current_error.take() {\n                errors.push(err);\n            }\n            if let Some(count) = parse_abort_count(line) {\n                error_count = Some(count);\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 5: Check for warning/error messages without error codes (unused, dead_code, etc.)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Check for unused warnings\n            if line.contains(\"unused\")\n                || line.contains(\"dead_code\")\n                || line.contains(\"unused_variables\")\n            {\n                // Save any current error before adding the general error\n                if let Some(err) = current_error.take() {\n                    errors.push(err);\n                }\n                errors.push(CompilationError::General {\n                    message: line.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // If we hit a blank line, save the current error\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(err) = current_error.take() {\n                errors.push(err);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Don't forget the last error if there was one\n    if let Some(err) = current_error {\n        errors.push(err);\n    }\n\n    // Add abort error if we detected one\n    if let Some(count) = error_count {\n        errors.push(CompilationError::Abort { error_count: count });\n    }\n\n    errors\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract error code and message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some((\"E0308\", \"mismatched types\"))\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {\n    if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n        if let Some(end_bracket) = line.find(']') {\n            let code = line[6..end_bracket].to_string(); // Skip \"error[\" but keep the \"E\"\n            let rest = line[end_bracket + 1..].trim();\n            let message = rest.strip_prefix(':').map(|s| s.trim()).unwrap_or(rest);\n            return Some((code, message.to_string()));\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Parse a location line to extract file, line, and column.\n///\n/// Input: \"   --> src/main.rs:10:5\"\n/// Output: Some((\"src/main.rs\", Some(10), Some(5)))\nfn parse_location_line(line: &str) -> Option<(String, Option<usize>, Option<usize>)> {\n    // Find the part after \"-->\"\n    if let Some(arrow_pos) = line.find(\"-->\") {\n        let location_part = line[arrow_pos + 3..].trim();\n\n        // Split by ':' to get file, line, and column\n        let parts: Vec<&str> = location_part.split(':').collect();\n\n        if parts.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let file = parts[0].trim().to_string();\n        let line_num = if parts.len() >= 2 {\n            parts[1].trim().parse().ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n        let column = if parts.len() >= 3 {\n            parts[2].trim().parse().ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        return Some((file, line_num, column));\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Parse the error count from an abort message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn parse_abort_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    for word in line.split_whitespace() {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Label utilities\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Extract labels suitable for propagation to child or related beads.\n///\n/// Returns labels that represent project/domain context. Excludes ephemeral\n/// state labels (\"in-progress\", \"ready\", \"alert\", \"crash\", \"signal-*\") that\n/// are set per-bead by NEEDLE and would be inappropriate on a derived bead.\npub fn extract_stitch_labels(labels: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {\n    const EXCLUDED: &[&str] = &[\n        \"alert\",\n        \"crash\",\n        \"in-progress\",\n        \"ready\",\n        \"blocked\",\n        \"done\",\n        \"closed\",\n    ];\n    labels\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|l| {\n            let lower = l.to_lowercase();\n            !EXCLUDED.contains(&lower.as_str()) && !lower.starts_with(\"signal-\")\n        })\n        .cloned()\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Extract only `stitch:`-prefixed labels for propagation to a derived bead\n/// (HOOP Hook 4 — Stitch Label Inheritance, docs/needle-hooks.md in the HOOP repo).\n///\n/// Unlike `extract_stitch_labels` (a blocklist that passes through nearly\n/// everything), this is a strict allowlist — it exists specifically so a\n/// follow-up bead inherits its parent's Stitch lineage without also picking\n/// up unrelated project/domain labels the parent happened to carry.\npub fn extract_stitch_prefixed_labels(labels: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {\n    labels\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|l| l.starts_with(\"stitch:\"))\n        .cloned()\n        .collect()\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Error Code Parsing and Classification Tests\n// let test_cases = vec![\n        (\"E0308\", ErrorCategory::TypeMismatch),\n        (\"E0382\", ErrorCategory::BorrowChecker),\n        (\"E0038\", ErrorCategory::TraitImpl),\n        (\"E0002\", ErrorCategory::PatternMatching),\n        (\"E0403\", ErrorCategory::ScopeVisibility),\n        (\"E0053\", ErrorCategory::Syntax),\n        (\"E0392\", ErrorCategory::Generic),\n        (\"E0276\", ErrorCategory::Macro),\n        (\"E0425\", ErrorCategory::DeadCode),\n        // Must be a well-formed but unmapped code. `parse_error_code` only\n        // accepts the E0xxx form that rustc actually emits — see\n        // `parse_error_code_invalid_format`, which asserts E1000/E2000 are\n        // rejected for exactly that reason. \"E9999\" therefore cannot parse,\n        // and category, expected_category,\n            \"Wrong category for {}: got {:?}, expected {:?}\",\n            code, category, expected_category\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Timeout Mitosis Decomposition Types\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mitosis mode: distinguishes timeout-triggered from ordinary failure decomposition.\n///\n/// Timeout mode uses different decomposition criteria and produces phase-based\n/// children that can close independently when their portion of work completes.\n/// Ordinary failure mode splits multi-task beads without phase awareness.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum MitosisMode {\n    /// Timeout-triggered mitosis: splits bead based on completed vs remaining work.\n    /// Uses timeout context (elapsed time, activity evidence, git state) to infer\n    /// decomposition boundaries and produce independently closable phases.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Ordinary failure mitosis: splits multi-task beads based on task analysis.\n    /// Triggered by failure count thresholds without timeout context.\n    Ordinary,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for MitosisMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            MitosisMode::Timeout => write!(f, \"timeout\"),\n            MitosisMode::Ordinary => write!(f, \"ordinary\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A child bead proposal in timeout-triggered mitosis.\n///\n/// Unlike ordinary mitosis children, timeout-phase They\n/// carry phase metadata and completion criteria.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub struct TimeoutPhaseProposal {\n    /// Human-readable title for this phase (e.g., \"Phase 1: Complete OAuth implementation\").\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Detailed description of what this phase accomplishes and its acceptance criteria.\n    pub description: String,\n    /// Whether this phase represents work already completed before the timeout.\n    /// Completed phases are created as closed beads to track progress without blocking.\n    pub is_completed: bool,\n    /// Dependencies on other phase beads by title (linearized by mitosis evaluator).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub depends_on_phases: Vec<String>,\n    /// Estimated or observed duration for this phase (if known).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub estimated_duration_secs: Option<u64>,\n    /// Completion criteria: what conditions must be met to close this phase bead.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub completion_criteria: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// A child bead proposal in ordinary failure mitosis.\n///\n/// Ordinary mitosis splits multi-task beads without phase awareness. Children\n/// are independent sub-tasks that must all complete before the parent closes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub struct represent either timeout or ordinary mode.\n///\n/// This enum provides type-safe discrimination between the two mitosis modes\n/// while maintaining a common API for the evaluator and Vec<TimeoutPhaseProposal>,\n        /// Reason if decomposition was refused (empty if proposing children).\n        #[serde(default)]\n        refusal_reason: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary DecompositionProposal::Timeout { phases, refusal_reason, .. } => {\n                refusal_reason.is_none() && !phases.is_empty()\n            }\n            DecompositionProposal::Ordinary { tasks, refusal_reason, .. } => {\n                refusal_reason.is_none() && !tasks.is_empty()\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the mitosis mode for this proposal.\n    pub fn mode(&self)  }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the refusal reason if decomposition was refused.\n    pub fn refusal_reason(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionProposal::Timeout {
